Rashi on Bava Batra 24b:10:1.hebrew: ומאי קושיא - מבור לעיר דאיצטריך לשנויי הכי? דלמא שאני היזק דרבים מהזיקא דיחיד: לא חייבו חכמים לקוץ אילנו בשביל בור היחיד בלא דמים, אבל בשביל היזק רבים חייבוהו לקוץ:
Rashi on Bava Batra 24b:10:1.english: And what is the difficulty? - [What is the difficulty] from [the case of] a pit [versus a tree] to [the case of] a city, such that it was necessary to resolve it this way? Perhaps damage to the public is different from damage to an individual: the Sages did not obligate [a person] to cut down his tree without compensation because of an individual's pit, but because of damage to the public they did obligate him to cut it down.

Rashi on Bava Batra 24b:11:1.hebrew: לא חמימא כו' - אם באת להמתין עד מתן מעות, יעמוד זה לאורך ימים; בני העיר סומכין זה על זה, ובעל האילן רוצה בכך. לפיכך יקוץ, ואחרי כן יגבה מעותיו מהן בב"ד:
Rashi on Bava Batra 24b:11:1.english: It is not hot, etc. - If you come to wait until the money is paid, this [tree] will remain standing for a long time; the townspeople rely on one another, and the owner of the tree wants this. Therefore, he should cut it down, and afterward he may collect his money from them in court.

Rashi on Bava Batra 24b:13:1.hebrew: התם - גבי בור, דודאי של אילן — אם ודאי קדם — לאו למיקץ קאי, כדקתני: "אם האילן קדם לא יקוץ". ספיקו נמי, לא אמר ליה "קוץ", שעל הניזק להביא ראיה:
Rashi on Bava Batra 24b:13:1.english: There - In the case of a pit [and a tree], where the certain case of the tree — if it certainly came first — [the tree] is not subject to being cut down, as the Mishnah teaches: "If the tree came first, he need not cut it down." In its doubtful case too, [the court] does not tell him "Cut [it] down," since the burden is on the one who was damaged to bring proof.

Rashi on Bava Batra 24b:13:2.english: Here, where [it is] certain - [the tree] also stands to be cut, except that [its owner] takes payment, as [the Mishnah] teaches: "If the tree was there first, he cuts [it] down and [the other party] pays him." In a case of its doubt as well, [the court] says to him [the tree owner]: "Cut [it down], since either way you have no choice." And when he comes to collect payment, [the other party] says to him: "Bring proof that you were there first, and [then] take [payment]."

Rashi on Bava Batra 24b:14:1.english: A fixed threshing floor - The Gemara explains what constitutes [its] fixedness.

Rashi on Bava Batra 24b:14:2.hebrew: חמשים אמה - מפני המוץ המזיק את בני העיר כשהוא זורה, וגם הזרעים הוא מייבש:
Rashi on Bava Batra 24b:14:2.english: Fifty cubits - Because of the chaff, which harms the people of the city when [the owner] winnows it, and it also dries out the seeds.

Rashi on Bava Batra 24b:14:3.hebrew: ומנירו של חבירו - ובגמרא מפרש: מאי היזק דמוץ לניר? ניר היא חרישה שחורשין בימי הקיץ, ואין זורעין בו עד ימות החורף, כדי שימותו שרשי הקוצים והעשבים, כדכתיב: "נירו לכם ניר ואל תזרעו אל קוצים" (ירמיהו ד׳:ג׳):
Rashi on Bava Batra 24b:14:3.english: And from the fallow field of his neighbor - And the Gemara explains: What damage does chaff cause to a fallow field? "Nir" is plowing that one plows during the summer days, and one does not sow it until the winter, so that the roots of the thorns and weeds will die, as it is written: "Break up your fallow ground, and do not sow among thorns" (Jeremiah 4:3).

Rashi on Bava Batra 24b:14:4.hebrew: בכדי שלא יזיק - האי שיעורא משמע בציר מחמשים אמה. ובגמרא פריך: מ"ש מרישא דאמרת "אלא אם כן יש לו חמשים אמה לכל רוח":
Rashi on Bava Batra 24b:14:4.english: Far enough that it will not cause damage - This measure implies less than fifty cubits. And in the Gemara it asks: What is different from the first clause, in which you said, "unless he has fifty cubits in every direction"?

Rashi on Bava Batra 24b:16:1.hebrew: שאינו זורה ברחת - שאין הכרי גדול, וא"צ לזרות ברחת, אלא הרוח מנשבת בכרי והמוץ נדף מאליו. רחת, פל"ה בלע"ז. כשהכרי גדול, צריך להגביה התבואה ברחת וזורק כלפי מעלה, והרוח מנשבת ודוחפת המוץ למרחוק:
Rashi on Bava Batra 24b:16:1.english: That he does not winnow with a winnowing shovel - Because the heap is not large, and there is no need to winnow with a winnowing shovel; rather, the wind blows on the heap and the chaff is carried off by itself. *Rachat* is *pala* in the vernacular (Old French). When the heap is large, one must lift the grain with a winnowing shovel and throw it upward, and the wind blows and drives the chaff far away.

Rashi on Bava Batra 24b:17:1.hebrew: רב אשי אמר - שיעורא דסיפא כרישא, ומה טעם קאמר:
Rashi on Bava Batra 24b:17:1.english: Rav Ashi said - The measure of the latter clause is the same as that of the first clause, and [Rav Ashi] states what the reason is.

Rashi on Bava Batra 24b:18:1.hebrew: מקשואיו ומדלועיו - נטיעה שהקשואין והדלועין גדילין בה:
Rashi on Bava Batra 24b:18:1.english: From its cucumbers and its gourds - [From] the planting in which the cucumbers and gourds grow.

Rashi on Bava Batra 24b:18:2.hebrew: בשלמא לרב אשי ניחא - דקתני בכולהו חמשים אמה:
Rashi on Bava Batra 24b:18:2.english: Granted, according to Rav Ashi it works well - For [the baraita] teaches "fifty cubits" in all of them.

Rashi on Bava Batra 24b:18:3.english: But according to Abaye, it is difficult - "It is difficult." This is how we read [the text].

Rashi on Bava Batra 24b:1:1.hebrew: דשפוכאי - שופכי יין מן החבית לנודות, למכור לעוברי דרכים במדינה זאת, כדמסיים ואזיל:
Rashi on Bava Batra 24b:1:1.english: Of the shefokhai - Those who pour wine from the barrel into wineskins to sell to travelers in this province, as [the Gemara] concludes and continues.

Rashi on Bava Batra 24b:1:2.hebrew: ברברבי - דליכא למיחש לרובא דעלמא, למימר מעוברי דרכים נפול:
Rashi on Bava Batra 24b:1:2.english: With regard to important people - For there is no need to worry about most of the world, [that one might say] that [the coins] fell from passersby.

Rashi on Bava Batra 24b:1:3.hebrew: ואי איכא רברבי בהדייהו - אף הקטנים מותרין, דברברבי לאו אורחייהו דעוברי דרכים, אלא כולהו מלוקח יין של מדינה זו נינהו, וישראל הן. וקטנים — שאין דרך ללוקח יין להביאם:
Rashi on Bava Batra 24b:1:3.english: And if there are large ones with them - Even the small ones are permitted, for it is not the way of passersby [to bring] large ones; rather, they all belong to the buyer of the wine of this town, and they are Jews. But small ones — it is not the way of a wine buyer to bring them.

Rashi on Bava Batra 24b:1:4.hebrew: אימור באברורי הוה מנחי - להשוות משא החמור. כשיש שתי נודות, זה גדול מזה מעט, ומכביד המשא לצד אחד — מניחין נוד קטן אצלו להשוות המשא:
Rashi on Bava Batra 24b:1:4.english: Say that they would place [them] as avrurei - [i.e.,] to even out the load of the donkey. When there are two skins, and one is slightly larger than the other and weighs the load down to one side, they place a small skin next to it in order to even out the load.

Rashi on Bava Batra 24b:2:1.hebrew: מרחיקין את האילן מן העיר - בגמרא מפרש משום נויי העיר, לפי שנוי לעיר כשיש מרחב פנוי לפניה:
Rashi on Bava Batra 24b:2:1.english: One must distance a tree from the city - The Gemara explains [that this is] because of the beautification of the city, since it is a beautification for a city when there is open space in front of it.

Rashi on Bava Batra 24b:2:2.english: A carob and a sycamore - Their branches are numerous.

Rashi on Bava Batra 24b:2:3.english: And a non-fruit-bearing tree - It is a disgrace to the city.

Rashi on Bava Batra 24b:2:4.english: And he gives [the value of the] money - The one whose city it is.

Rashi on Bava Batra 24b:3:1.hebrew: ותיפוק ליה דאין עושין מגרש שדה - משנה היא בפ' אחרון של ערכין (דף לג:). ומגרש אלף אמה הוא, וכל אלף אמה אסור לעשותו שדה, וקס"ד לא שדה לבן ולא שדה אילן:
Rashi on Bava Batra 24b:3:1.english: And let him derive it from [the fact] that one may not turn a open land [migrash] into a field - This is a Mishnah in the last chapter of Arakhin (33b). And a migrash is a thousand cubits, and it is forbidden to make any [part of the] thousand cubits into a field. And the initial assumption was [that this applies to] neither a grain field nor a tree field.

Rashi on Bava Batra 24b:4:1.hebrew: לא צריכא לר' אלעזר - דפליג התם ואמר: בד"א בערי הלוים, אבל בערי ישראל כו':
Rashi on Bava Batra 24b:4:1.english: It is not necessary, [except] according to Rabbi Elazar - who disagrees there and says: When does this apply? In the cities of the Levites; but in the cities of Israel, etc.

Rashi on Bava Batra 24b:5:1.hebrew: ה"ג ולרבנן דאמרי אין עושין הני מילי בזרעים אבל באילנות עושין - בתוך אלף אמה:
Rashi on Bava Batra 24b:5:1.english: This is the text we read: "And according to the Rabbis, who say: One may not [make a field into an open space] — this applies to seeds, but with trees, one may [do so]" - Within a thousand cubits.

Rashi on Bava Batra 24b:5:2.english: And here - Within twenty-five cubits, because of the beautification of the city, one may not do so.

Rashi on Bava Batra 24b:6:1.hebrew: קרפף יותר מבית סאתים שהוקף לדירה - סאתים הוא שיעור חצר המשכן, ונתנוהו חכמים שיעור לכל היקף שלא הוקף לדור בתוכו, או להשתמש מן הבית לתוכו, כגון קרפף שבבקעה. אבל המוקף לדירה, אפי' בית עשרה כורין, מטלטלין בו. וקאמר הכא: יתר מבית סאתים שהוקף לדירה, הוא מותר לטלטל בכולו:
Rashi on Bava Batra 24b:6:1.english: A karpef larger than a beit se'atayim that was enclosed for dwelling - Two se'ah is the size of the courtyard of the Tabernacle, and the Sages established it as the measure for any enclosure that was not enclosed for living in it, or for using [it] from the house into it, such as a karpef in a valley. But [an area] enclosed for dwelling, even [of] a beit of ten kor, one may carry in it. And [the baraita] says here: [A karpef] larger than a beit se'atayim that was enclosed for dwelling — it is permitted to carry throughout all of it.

Rashi on Bava Batra 24b:7:1.hebrew: נזרע רובו - בטלו הזרעים שם דירה ממנו, והרי הוא כגינה, שאין הקפה לדירה. הואיל ויתר מבית סאתים הוא, אין מטלטלין בו עוד:
Rashi on Bava Batra 24b:7:1.english: Most of it was sown - The crops nullified its status as a dwelling area, and it is like a garden, for there is no enclosure for dwelling [purposes]. Since it is larger than a beit se'atayim, one may no longer carry in it.

Rashi on Bava Batra 24b:7:2.hebrew: אבל ניטע רובו - באילנות, אין האילנות מבטלין תורת דירתו ממנו, והרי הוא כחצר שלפני הבתים שהקיפוה לדירה, ומותר:
Rashi on Bava Batra 24b:7:2.english: But if the majority of it was planted - with trees: the trees do not nullify its status as a dwelling area, and it is like the courtyard in front of houses that was enclosed for dwelling, and it is permitted.

Rashi on Bava Batra 24b:8:1.hebrew: מאי שנא בור - דבעינן נמי הרחקה, וקתני נמי: אם הבור קדמה, קוצץ, ונותן בעל הבור דמי האילן לבעל האילן:
Rashi on Bava Batra 24b:8:1.english: What is different about a pit - [That is,] for we also require distancing [there], and it also teaches: if the pit came first, [the tree owner] cuts [the tree down], and the owner of the pit gives the value of the tree to the owner of the tree.

Rashi on Bava Batra 24b:9:1.hebrew: לא חמימא ולא קרירא - שזה סומך על זה. אף כאן, דמי האילן מי יתנם? אם באת להטילם על בני העיר, כל אחד אומר: ממני לא יתחילו! ונמצא האילן עומד והעיר מגונה, ואין זו תפארת ארץ ישראל:
Rashi on Bava Batra 24b:9:1.english: Neither hot nor cold - For each one relies on the other. Here too, who will pay the value of the tree? If you come to impose it on the townspeople, each one says, "Let them not begin with me!" And the result is that the tree remains standing and the city is disfigured, and this is not the beauty of the Land of Israel.

Tosafot on Bava Batra 24b:11:1.hebrew: ולימא להו הבו לי ברישא והדר איקוץ - גבי בור לא שייך למיפרך הכי, דניחא: כיון שסמך באיסור, שיקוץ תחלה:
Tosafot on Bava Batra 24b:11:1.english: "And let him say to them: Give me [payment] first, and then I will cut" - With regard to a pit, it is not relevant to raise this objection, for it is reasonable [that] since he relied on a prohibited act, he should cut first.

Tosafot on Bava Batra 24b:18:1.hebrew: קשיא לאביי - תימה: מאי קשיא ליה? הא ברייתא איירי בגורן קבוע, ומתניתין בגורן שאינו קבוע! ויש לומר דאביי גופיה הוה משני דמה טעם קאמר; אי לאו משום דקשיא ליה — מה צריך לפרש טעמא? כדי שלא יזיק. והשתא דבברייתא מפרש טעמא כדי שלא יזיק, מתני' נמי איכא לפרושי הכי:
Tosafot on Bava Batra 24b:18:1.english: It was difficult for Abaye - It is puzzling: What was difficult for him? The baraita is speaking about a fixed threshing floor, whereas the Mishnah is speaking about a threshing floor that is not fixed! And one can answer that Abaye himself was the one who answered [earlier] that [Rabbi Yose] stated "what is the reason" [as a distinct question]. If it were not because [the matter] was difficult for him, why would it need to explain the reason? [The answer is:] so that it should not cause damage. And now that in the baraita the reason is explained as being so that it should not cause damage, the Mishnah too can be explained in this way.

Tosafot on Bava Batra 24b:2:1.hebrew: מרחיקין את האילן [מן העיר] כ"ה אמה - וזרעים צריך להרחיק מן העיר עד אלף אמה, דאין עושין מגרש שדה:
Tosafot on Bava Batra 24b:2:1.english: “They distance a tree [from the city] twenty-five cubits” - But [with regard to] crops, one must distance them from the city up to a thousand cubits, since one may not turn a [city’s] open space into a field.

Tosafot on Bava Batra 24b:9:1.hebrew: מ"ש מבור דקוצץ ונותן דמים אמר רב כהנא קידרא דבי שותפי כו' - תימה לרשב"א: א"כ, כשהאילן קדם נמי, אמאי נותן דמים מהאי טעמא? וי"ל, דכשהאילן קדם, כיון דסמך בהיתר, אין לחוש אם יתעצלו וישאר האילן עומד. אבל עוד קשה לו: דמאי שייך הכא "קידרא דבי שותפי"? והלא קוצץ תחלה קודם שיתנו דמים! ואומר ר"י, דה"פ: דמשום "קידרא דבי שותפי לא חיימא ולא קרירא" לא רצו לתקן שיתנו דמים; דאע"ג דקוצץ תחלה, פעמים שלא ישמע להם לקוץ תחלה אם לא ידע מי יתן לו הדמים, וכל אחד ואחד יתרשל ולא יקוץ כדי שלא ליתן דמים, כי בעל האילן ידרוש מעמו:
Tosafot on Bava Batra 24b:9:1.english: How is this different from a pit, where he cuts down [the tree] and pays [the owner of the tree]? Rav Kahana said: "A pot of partners..." etc. - The Rashba found this puzzling: If so, then even when the tree came first, why should [the one who built the city or field] pay the value, for this same reason? And one can answer that when the tree came first, since [the other] relied on a permitted situation, there is no concern that they will be lazy and the tree will remain standing. But [the Rashba] had another difficulty: What does "a pot of partners" have to do with this case? Doesn't he cut down [the tree] first, before they pay the value? And Rabbeinu Yitzchak says that this is what [the Gemara] means: Because of [the principle that] "a pot of partners is neither hot nor cold," they did not want to institute that [the townspeople] should pay. For even though he cuts down [the tree] first, there are times that [the tree's owner] will not agree to cut it down first if he does not know who will give him the money. And each and every one [of the townspeople] will be lazy and will not cut it down, so as not to have to pay, since the owner of the tree will demand [payment] from him.
